coreConcept: Role of Endoscopic Ultrasound in Pancreatic Cancer
statement: A multidisciplinary team (MDT) is planning the staging investigations for a 58-year-old male with a suspected pancreatic mass. Which imaging modality is most useful for achieving high-resolution staging and guiding biopsy probes in this specific anatomic location?
options: Non-contrast computed tomography of the abdomen
optionExplanations: Pelvic MRI is used for rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers, not primarily for the pancreas.
Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) is specifically highlighted as helpful for staging pancreatic cancers and allows for precise biopsy.
Standard transabdominal ultrasound is less sensitive than EUS for detailed pancreatic staging.
PET visualizes metabolic activity but is less effective for local anatomic staging compared to EUS in the pancreas.
CT is useful but endoscopic ultrasound provides higher resolution for local staging and allows for simultaneous biopsy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Endoscopic ultrasound is helpful in staging upper gastrointestinal and pancreatic cancers, involving a special endoscope with an ultrasound and biopsy probe attached.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Investigation of Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO)
statement: A 62-year-old heavy smoker presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of progressive breathlessness, facial fullness, and swelling of both arms. Physical examination reveals distended, non-pulsatile neck veins and a dusky coloration of the face. A chest X-ray shows a large right-sided mediastinal mass. What is the most appropriate next step in the diagnostic workup to confirm the suspected underlying emergency?
options: Bilateral brachial venography to map the venous occlusion
Measurement of serum lactate dehydrogenase and uric acid
Urgent computed tomography scan of the thoracic cavity
Immediate fine-needle aspiration of the distended neck veins
Emergency isotope bone scan to check for thoracic spread
correctOption: Urgent computed tomography scan of the thoracic cavity
optionExplanations: Brachial venography is invasive and has been largely replaced by CT as the first-line investigation for SVCO.
These markers are relevant for tumor lysis syndrome, not for characterizing an anatomical vascular obstruction like SVCO.

The patient's symptoms (facial edema, distended neck veins, breathlessness) indicate Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO). CT thorax is the gold-standard investigation to confirm this and identify the cause.
FNA is used for tissue diagnosis, but anatomical confirmation of the obstruction via imaging is the priority in an emergency.
A bone scan would not address the acute vascular obstruction suggested by the clinical presentation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): [The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: RAS Mutations and EGFR Inhibitor Resistance
statement: Molecular profiling of a biopsy specimen from a 68-year-old female with metastatic colorectal cancer reveals a KRAS mutation. How does this specific investigation influence the subsequent management plan for this patient?
options: It indicates that the tumor will respond well to HER2 inhibitors
It necessitates the use of high-dose cytotoxic alkylating agents
It predicts resistance to targeted therapy with EGFR inhibitors
It suggests that the patient is eligible for ALK fusion inhibitors
It confirms high microsatellite instability and immune response
correctOption: It predicts resistance to targeted therapy with EGFR inhibitors
optionExplanations: HER2 inhibitors are primarily used in breast or gastric cancers, not dictated by KRAS status in colon cancer.
The choice of cytotoxic agents like alkylating drugs is not primarily guided by KRAS status.
In colorectal cancer, the presence of RAS (KRAS/NRAS) mutations predicts resistance to EGFR inhibitors like cetuximab or panitumumab.
ALK fusion rearrangements are typically investigated in lung cancer, not colorectal cancer.
Microsatellite instability is a separate molecular investigation from KRAS mutational status.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the TNM classification system for staging malignant tumors, how should a clinician interpret a finding of 'NX' following a staging evaluation?
options: Regional lymph nodes could not be clinically assessed
Metastasis to distant organs has been confirmed
No regional lymph node involvement was detected
There is no clinical evidence of any primary tumor
The tumor size exceeds the maximum T4 measurement
correctOption: Regional lymph nodes could not be clinically assessed
optionExplanations: In the TNM system, 'X' denotes that the specific category (Tumor, Node, or Metastasis) could not be assessed.
Confirmed distant metastasis is denoted as M1.
No nodal involvement is denoted as N0.
No evidence of primary tumor is denoted as T0.
Tumor size is denoted by the T category (T1-T4), not by the X prefix.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): [NX Not assessed]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: During the evaluation of a patient's response to systemic anti-cancer therapy using the RECIST (Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours), the oncologist notes a 25% increase in the sum of the longest diameters of target lesions. How is this response classified?
optionExplanations: According to RECIST, an increase of at least 20% in the sum of the longest diameters is classified as progressive disease.
Stable disease is for changes that do not meet the criteria for PR or PD.
Partial response requires at least a 30% decrease.
Complete response requires the disappearance of all target lesions.
'Metastatic escape' is not a standard RECIST classification term.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 149 (Book Page): [Progressive disease (PD) At least a 20% increase in the sum of the LD of target lesions]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Initial Workup for Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP)
statement: A 55-year-old male is found to have multi-organ metastatic disease involving the liver and bone, but no primary site is identified after initial history and physical examination. According to clinical protocols for Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP), which initial diagnostic battery is most appropriate for this patient if he is fit for investigation?
options: Exploratory laparotomy and whole-body radioactive iodine scan
CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with a biopsy of the most accessible site
Immediate initiation of generic cytotoxic chemotherapy without further imaging
Sequential upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopies followed by MRI brain
Serial measurement of all known serum tumor markers prior to any imaging
correctOption: CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with a biopsy of the most accessible site
optionExplanations: Laparotomy is invasive and not an initial diagnostic step; iodine scans are specific to thyroid cancer.
The standard initial workup for CUP includes detailed CT imaging of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, along with obtaining tissue for pathology from the most accessible lesion.
Investigations should be performed first to identify potentially treatable or favorable CUP subtypes.
Endoscopies are only indicated if there are specific localizing symptoms or radiological suspicion.
Imaging is prioritized alongside core labs; tumor markers are interpreted within the context of clinical and imaging findings.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): [Initial diagnostic tests in patients presenting with carcinoma of unknown primary... CT scan of chest, abdomen and pelvis... Histological examination by biopsy]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 70-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer is found to have a total serum calcium level of 2.8 mmol/L. Her serum albumin is 20 g/L (Normal 35–50 g/L). Why is it clinically essential to calculate the corrected calcium in this patient?
options: High albumin levels usually mask the symptoms of hypercalcaemia
Hypoalbuminaemia leads to an underestimation of the ionized calcium
Total calcium measurement is technically inaccurate in bone metastasis
Renal failure in cancer patients alters the calcium-albumin ratio
Hypercalcaemia of malignancy is exclusively caused by bound calcium
correctOption: Hypoalbuminaemia leads to an underestimation of the ionized calcium
optionExplanations: High albumin is rare in cancer; hypoalbuminaemia is the common clinical issue that masks hypercalcaemia.
Most calcium is bound to albumin. In hypoalbuminaemia, the total calcium appears lower, but the physiologically active (ionized) portion may be dangerously high, necessitating a correction.
The measurement itself is accurate, but its clinical interpretation depends on protein levels.
Renal failure affects calcium levels but the primary reason for correction in oncology is the low albumin state.
Hypercalcaemia is caused by an increase in free ionized calcium, not just bound calcium.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 143 (Book Page): [It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient's laboratory report indicates a significantly elevated serum calcitonin level. This biochemical marker is most useful for the screening and monitoring of which specific oncological condition?
options: Papillary adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic duct
Medullary cell carcinoma of the thyroid gland
Non-seminomatous germ cell tumors of the ovary
correctOption: Medullary cell carcinoma of the thyroid gland
optionExplanations: CA 19.9 is associated with pancreatic cancer.
MALT lymphomas are diagnosed by biopsy and linked to H. pylori, not calcitonin.
AFP is the marker for hepatocellular carcinoma.
Calcitonin is the classic tumor marker for medullary thyroid cancer and is also used to screen for MEN 2.
AFP and hCG are the markers for germ cell tumors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): [Calcitonin... Medullary cell carcinoma of thyroid]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 28-year-old male presents with a rapidly enlarging painless testicular mass. Initial laboratory screening reveals a significantly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) level. Which of the following neoplasms is most specifically associated with this biochemical finding?
optionExplanations: Prostate cancer is monitored via PSA (Prostate-specific antigen), not AFP.
Choriocarcinoma is classically associated with high levels of hCG, not AFP.
Seminomas typically do not produce AFP; they may occasionally show mild elevations of hCG or PLAP.
Ovarian dysgerminoma is the female equivalent of seminoma and is typically associated with PLAP, not AFP.
AFP is a glycoprotein found in fetal tissue; its elevation in a young male with a germ cell tumor is highly suggestive of non-seminomatous elements or teratoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) favour germ-cell tumours. Page 138 (Book Page): Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%), hepatocellular cancer (50%).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A clinical oncologist is planning to evaluate a patient for potential distant metastases using Positron Emission Tomography (PET-CT). Which physiological principle best explains the primary limitation of this modality in oncological staging?
options: Malignant lymph nodes may lack sufficient metabolic activity for detection.
The radioactive half-life of tracers prevents multi-organ visualization.
Ionizing radiation from CT components obscures metabolic signal intensity.
The spatial resolution of PET scanners exceeds that of modern CT units.
Metabolic tracers are unable to cross the blood-brain barrier effectively.
correctOption: Malignant lymph nodes may lack sufficient metabolic activity for detection.
optionExplanations: PET-CT relies on metabolic activity (PET-avidity); if a tumor is small or has low metabolic turnover, it may result in a false-negative finding.
Standard protocols allow for whole-body imaging despite the half-life of tracers like Fluorine-18.
PET and CT are complementary; the CT component actually helps with anatomical localization and attenuation correction.
The resolution is generally lower in PET compared to CT; the limitation is biological/metabolic, not resolution-based in this context.
Standard PET tracers like FDG are commonly used to visualize high-metabolic areas including the brain.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): Not all tumour types are ‘PET-avid’ and the metabolic activity of small but malignant lymph nodes may not be detected, limiting the sensitivity of PET-CT.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the diagnostic workup of a core biopsy from a breast mass, immunohistochemical (IHC) staining is performed. How does the clinical significance of HER2 receptor positivity contrast with that of Oestrogen Receptor (ER) positivity?
options: HER2 status identifies the primary site whereas ER status predicts distant metastasis.
HER2 indicates hormone sensitivity whereas ER status indicates drug resistance.
HER2 reflects the tumor's grade whereas ER reflects the tumor's size and stage.
HER2 positivity suggests a benign origin whereas ER positivity suggests malignancy.
HER2 predicts response to targeted inhibitors whereas ER predicts hormone sensitivity.
correctOption: HER2 predicts response to targeted inhibitors whereas ER predicts hormone sensitivity.
optionExplanations: Both can be used to help identify primary sites, but their primary clinical role is therapeutic stratification.
ER status indicates hormone sensitivity, while HER2 is a target for specific biological therapies.
While HER2 can correlate with more aggressive biology, neither specifically defines the TNM stage.
Both ER and HER2 are assessed in malignant tissues to guide treatment.
ER/PR positivity suggests the tumor will respond to drugs like tamoxifen, while HER2 positivity suggests response to trastuzumab.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation... HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Management of Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP) with Poor Prognostic Features
statement: A 68-year-old male with a 50-pack-year smoking history presents with a 15 kg weight loss, persistent abdominal fullness, and fatigue. Physical examination reveals an enlarged, firm, non-tender liver and left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy (Virchow’s node). Laboratory studies show a low serum albumin of 2.8 g/dL and a C-reactive protein (CRP) of 85 mg/L. A CT scan confirms multiple liver and lung nodules but fails to identify a primary tumor. He is currently bed-bound for approximately 60% of his waking hours. What is the most appropriate next step in the diagnostic management of this patient?
options: Obtain a core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic nodal lesion.
Prioritize palliative care and discuss goals of care with the patient.
Perform an urgent PET-CT to 'hunt down' the elusive primary malignancy.
Schedule an immediate colonoscopy to evaluate for a gastrointestinal primary.
Initiate empiric cytotoxic chemotherapy for suspected small cell cancer.
correctOption: Prioritize palliative care and discuss goals of care with the patient.
optionExplanations: While biopsy is standard for fit patients, this patient has PS 3 and biochemical markers suggesting very poor prognosis.
The combination of PS 3, multi-organ spread, low albumin, and high CRP indicates a very short prognosis where palliative care takes priority over invasive diagnostics.
Hunting for a primary site is often not beneficial in patients with poor performance status and poor prognostic markers.
Specialist investigations like colonoscopy are only indicated if there are specific localizing symptoms or radiological suspicion.
Empiric chemotherapy is not indicated without a tissue diagnosis and assessment of fitness for treatment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): Features associated with poor prognosis... include: poor performance status (PS 3–4), requirement for hospital admission, bulky or multi-organ metastatic disease... raised inflammatory markers and low albumin. Further investigations, including biopsy, may not be warranted and honest conversations about palliative care and end-of-life planning are often preferable.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 64-year-old patient with multiple myeloma is admitted for severe hypercalcaemia. While administering intravenous 0.9% saline to improve renal function, the medical team prepares to give intravenous bisphosphonates. Which mechanistic aspect of bisphosphonate therapy is critical to communicate to the clinical team regarding its time-course of action?
options: It causes rapid intracellular shifts of calcium into the skeletal matrix.
It induces rapid calcium excretion through the kidneys within six hours.
It acts as a PTHrP antagonist to stop osteoclastic stimulation instantly.
It inhibits bone resorption with maximal effect reached within five days.
It provides an immediate dilutional effect on the extracellular fluid.
correctOption: It inhibits bone resorption with maximal effect reached within five days.
optionExplanations: Bisphosphonates inhibit the breakdown of bone rather than promoting active 'pumping' of calcium back into bone.
Renal excretion is handled by saline; bisphosphonates act on the bone.
Bisphosphonates do not antagonize PTHrP; they physically inhibit osteoclastic resorption.
Bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclast activity but have a delayed clinical effect, typically taking several days to normalize calcium.
The dilutional effect is achieved by intravenous saline, not bisphosphonates.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 143 (Book Page): Patients should initially be treated with intravenous 0.9% saline to improve renal function... Bisphosphonates will usually reduce the serum calcium levels to normal within 5 days.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: During a multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting, a patient is described as being capable of only limited self-care and is confined to a bed or chair for approximately 70% of his waking hours. Which Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status grade best fits this description?
options: Grade 4: Completely disabled and totally confined
Grade 3: Confined for more than 50% of waking hours
Grade 2: Ambulatory and capable of self-care
correctOption: Grade 3: Confined for more than 50% of waking hours
optionExplanations: Grade 0 implies no restrictions at all.
Grade 1 means the patient is ambulatory and able to do light work.
Grade 4 means the patient is 100% confined and unable to carry out any self-care.
Grade 3 specifically matches the description of being confined to a bed/chair more than 50% of the time with limited self-care.
Grade 2 means the patient is up and about more than 50% of waking hours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): 3 Capable of only limited self-care, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Investigation of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression
statement: A 55-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer presents with a three-day history of rapidly worsening band-like back pain that is most severe when she is lying flat. On examination, she has increased knee reflexes and extensor plantar reflexes. What is the most appropriate investigative step to confirm the suspected diagnosis?
options: Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis for staging.
Bone scintigraphy to detect areas of high osteoblastic turnover.
Plain X-ray of the lumbar spine to check for vertebral body collapse.
CT-guided biopsy of the most tender thoracic vertebral segment.
Urgent MRI scan of the whole spine to assess for cord compression.
correctOption: Urgent MRI scan of the whole spine to assess for cord compression.
optionExplanations: CT is useful for staging but MRI is superior for evaluating the spinal cord and soft tissue extension of tumors.
Bone scans detect turnover but do not provide the detail needed to confirm cord compression.
Plain X-rays are insensitive to early cord compression and cannot visualize the cord itself.
Biopsy is secondary to confirming the compression and relieving it.
MRI is the gold standard; whole-spine imaging is required as multiple levels of compression can occur simultaneously.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’... Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Investigation of Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO)
statement: A 62-year-old female smoker presents with facial plethora, swelling of the arms, and prominent, non-pulsatile distension of the neck veins. She reports a dull headache that worsens when she stoops forward to tie her shoes. Her chest X-ray shows a large right-sided mediastinal mass. Which investigation is most critical to distinguish if her clinical presentation is due to extrinsic tumor compression or an intravascular thrombus associated with her central venous catheter?
options: Serial measurement of serum BNP to rule out congestive heart failure.
Transthoracic echocardiography to evaluate for pericardial effusion.
Computed Tomography (CT) scan of the thorax with contrast.
Fine needle aspiration (FNA) of the palpable neck veins for cytology.
Positron Emission Tomography to determine tumor metabolic avidity.
correctOption: Computed Tomography (CT) scan of the thorax with contrast.
optionExplanations: BNP rules out heart failure but the presentation (distended non-pulsatile JVP, facial swelling) is classic for SVCO.
Echocardiography evaluates the heart; it does not directly visualize the superior vena cava in enough detail to distinguish SVCO causes.
CT thorax with contrast is the diagnostic standard to visualize the SVC, identify compression by a mass, or see an internal thrombus.
FNA is for tissue diagnosis (tumor type), not for confirming the cause of vascular obstruction.
PET helps with staging but CT is the primary tool for anatomical evaluation of the obstruction itself.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient with bulky High-Grade Lymphoma is started on aggressive cytotoxic chemotherapy. Within 24 hours, the medical team monitors for Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS). According to standard clinical monitoring, which of the following typically serves as the earliest biochemical marker of this syndrome?
options: Hyperuricaemia resulting from the breakdown of nucleic acids.
Pre-treatment serum LDH as a surrogate for total tumor bulk.
Elevated serum potassium released from the destroyed tumor cells.
Hypocalcaemia due to calcium precipitation with phosphate ions.
Acute elevation of serum creatinine indicating renal impairment.
correctOption: Elevated serum potassium released from the destroyed tumor cells.
optionExplanations: Hyperuricaemia is a key component of TLS but may develop slightly later as purines are metabolized.
LDH is a marker of bulk and risk, but not a marker of the acute onset of the syndrome itself.
Potassium is the most abundant intracellular cation; its rapid release into the blood is often the first sign of massive cell lysis.
Hypocalcaemia is a clinical feature of TLS but usually follows the rise in phosphate.
Renal impairment (creatinine rise) is a consequence of uric acid and phosphate crystals, not the primary early marker of lysis itself.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 143 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium... Elevated serum potassium may be the earliest biochemical marker.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A pathologist is reviewing immunohistochemical (IHC) slides for a tumor of unknown origin. Positive staining for which of the following markers would most strongly favour a diagnosis of an epithelial carcinoma over other tumor types?
options: T-cell receptor and cluster designation (CD) antigens
Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and HER2 receptor protein
optionExplanations: AFP and hCG are markers specifically favoring germ-cell tumors.
ER/PR suggest a specific origin (breast/uterus) rather than classifying the tumor broadly as a carcinoma.
CD antigens are the hallmark markers for lymphomas and leukemias.
PSA is specific to prostate origin, and HER2 is an oncogenic target, not a general marker for all carcinomas.
Cytokeratins and EMA are structural proteins characteristic of epithelial cells, making them the primary markers for carcinomas.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): Cytokeratins and epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) favour epithelial carcinomas.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Which imaging modality is recognized as the standard technique for the initial staging of rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers due to its high resolution in pelvic structures?
options: Trans-rectal or trans-vaginal ultrasound of the pelvic organs
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the pelvis
Positron emission tomography coupled with computed tomography
Radio-isotope bone scintigraphy for local pelvic involvement
High-resolution magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvis
correctOption: High-resolution magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvis
optionExplanations: Ultrasound is useful for characterising lesions in organs like the liver or kidney but is not the primary staging tool for rectal or cervical cancer.
CT is primarily used for the thorax and abdomen rather than specialized pelvic staging where high resolution is needed.
PET-CT is used for metabolic activity and distant metastases, not for the primary local staging of these pelvic cancers.
Bone scintigraphy is used to detect skeletal metastases, not for the local staging of the primary tumor site in the pelvis.
Correct. MRI is the preferred modality for pelvic imaging, including rectal and prostate staging, due to its superior soft tissue resolution.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A radiologist reports a PET-CT finding of metabolic activity in a mediastinal mass. What is a primary physiological limitation of this investigation that requires careful interpretation in the clinical staging of malignancy?
options: It is unable to provide anatomical localization of metabolically active sites
It cannot distinguish between visceral organs and tumor masses
It identifies only anaerobic metabolism within high-grade necrotic tumors
It lacks sensitivity for detecting small malignant lymph node involvement
It requires the patient to be in a fasting state for over twenty-four hours
correctOption: It lacks sensitivity for detecting small malignant lymph node involvement
optionExplanations: PET-CT specifically provides anatomical localization by combining the metabolic data of PET with the structural data of CT.
PET-CT is specifically designed to distinguish tumor activity within various anatomical structures.
PET-CT visualizes glucose metabolism (typically aerobic glycolysis in cancers), not exclusively anaerobic metabolism.
Correct. PET-CT has limited sensitivity for detecting small but malignant lymph nodes, which can lead to false-negative staging.
While fasting is required, the primary clinical limitation mentioned in the text is the detection threshold for small malignant nodes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): Not all tumour types are ‘PET-avid’ and the metabolic activity of small but malignant lymph nodes may not be detected, limiting the sensitivity of PET-CT.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A clinician monitors a patient with a known mucinous tumor of the ovary. Which serum tumor marker is most frequently elevated in this specific malignancy, but is also known to rise in the presence of any cause of cholestasis?
optionExplanations: AFP is used for germ cell tumors and hepatocellular cancer, not primarily for mucinous ovarian tumors.
hCG is used for choriocarcinoma and germ cell tumors, not mucinous ovarian epithelial tumors.
Correct. CA-19.9 is associated with mucinous ovarian tumors and its levels are confounded by cholestasis because it is eliminated via bile.
PLAP is an isoenzyme used primarily for seminoma and ovarian dysgerminoma.
CEA is elevated in colorectal and gastric cancers, but its elimination is not specifically tied to bile in a way that cholestasis is a primary diagnostic confounder in this context.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): CA-19.9... Pancreatic cancer (80%), mucinous tumour of the ovary (65%)... It is eliminated exclusively via bile and so any degree of cholestasis can cause levels to rise

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 72-year-old male with a 50 pack-year smoking history presents with profound fatigue, 12 kg weight loss over three months, and jaundice. Physical examination reveals an ECOG performance status of 3. Laboratory studies show a serum albumin of 21 g/L and a C-reactive protein of 165 mg/L. CT imaging demonstrates multiple liver, lung, and bone metastases with no identifiable primary. What is the most appropriate management approach for this patient?
options: Proceed with an urgent ultrasound-guided core biopsy of the liver
Request a whole-body PET-CT to hunt down the primary occult tumor
Focus on palliative care and end-of-life planning without further testing
Initiate broad-spectrum cytotoxic chemotherapy for unknown primary
Perform a diagnostic laparoscopy to locate the primary malignancy
correctOption: Focus on palliative care and end-of-life planning without further testing
optionExplanations: While a biopsy helps define tumor type, in a patient with PS 3 and poor prognostic labs, investigations may not be in the patient's best interest.
Hunting for a primary tumor is not indicated when the patient's fitness and clinical markers suggest that treatment would not be feasible or beneficial.
Correct. The combination of PS 3, low albumin, and high inflammatory markers indicates a very poor prognosis where palliative care is the most appropriate step.
Chemotherapy is generally not indicated for patients with a performance status of 3 or 4 as it is poorly tolerated and unlikely to benefit.
Invasive surgical procedures like laparoscopy are inappropriate for a patient with PS 3 and multi-organ metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): Features associated with poor prognosis... include: poor performance status (PS 3–4), requirement for hospital admission, bulky or multi-organ metastatic disease, signiﬁcant comorbidity, raised LDH, raised inﬂammatory markers and low albumin. Further investigations, including biopsy, may not be warranted and honest conversations about palliative care and end-of-life planning are often preferable.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Molecular profiling of a colorectal tumor is requested to guide systemic therapy. Which specific molecular investigation is essential to predict resistance to Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) inhibitor targeted therapy?
options: Assessment of RAS family gene mutation status
Testing for EGFR activating mutations in the kinase domain
Testing for ALK fusion oncogene rearrangements
correctOption: Assessment of RAS family gene mutation status
optionExplanations: MSI predicts response to checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy, not resistance to EGFR inhibitors.
Correct. RAS mutations in colon cancer specifically predict resistance to anti-EGFR therapies like cetuximab.
EGFR mutations are used to predict response in lung cancer; in colon cancer, RAS status is the critical predictor for anti-EGFR therapy resistance.
ALK rearrangements are used to predict response in lung cancer, not resistance in colon cancer.
HER2 over-expression is used to predict response to targeted therapy in breast and gastric cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: When utilizing the International Union against Cancer (UICC) TNM staging system, which parameter is used to describe the extent or depth of invasion of the primary tumor itself?
optionExplanations: NX indicates that the regional lymph nodes could not be assessed.
The 'N' parameter (N1-N3) describes the increasing involvement of regional lymph nodes.
Correct. The 'T' parameter (T1-T4) describes the increasing size or local extent/depth of the primary tumor.
MX indicates that the presence of distant metastases was not assessed.
M0 indicates that no distant metastases are present.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): T1, T2, T3, T4... Increase in primary tumour size or depth of invasion

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A clinician is performing a fine needle aspiration (FNA) of a palpable neck lump. According to standard procedural guidelines, what finding in the syringe hub indicates that the procedure should be stopped immediately to preserve sample quality?
options: Appearance of blood in the hub
correctOption: Appearance of blood in the hub
optionExplanations: Serous fluid does not necessitate stopping; it might be part of the sample in cystic lesions.
Mucoid material is often diagnostic for certain types of tumors and is not a reason to stop.
The goal is to obtain material; if none is seen, the clinician usually continues to make passes unless blood appears.
Correct. Blood contamination dilutes the cellular material and reduces the quality of the cytological evaluation.
Resistance is expected as negative pressure is a part of the aspiration technique to obtain cells.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): Stop sampling if blood is seen in the syringe hub as blood reduces the quality of the sample.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 58-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer presents with new-onset, severe thoracic back pain that worsens when coughing or lying flat. On examination, she has symmetrical lower limb weakness and increased knee reflexes. What is the single most important next step in the investigation of this suspected oncological emergency?
options: Urgent magnetic resonance imaging scan of the whole spine
Serum calcium measurement to rule out symptomatic hypercalcaemia
Isotope bone scan to identify high-uptake areas in the vertebrae
Plain film radiographs to check for vertebral wedge fractures
Computed tomography of the thoracic spine with contrast enhancement
correctOption: Urgent magnetic resonance imaging scan of the whole spine
optionExplanations: Correct. Urgent MRI of the whole spine is the gold standard investigation for malignant spinal cord compression to visualize all possible sites of compression.
While hypercalcaemia causes non-specific symptoms, it does not explain the focal neurological deficits and upper motor neuron signs seen here.
Bone scans lack the resolution to confirm cord compression and may have false positives/negatives.
X-rays cannot visualize the spinal cord or identify early compression; they only show bone changes.
CT is less sensitive than MRI for visualizing soft tissue compression of the spinal cord.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): Management of suspected spinal cord compression... Conﬁrm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the biochemical investigation of a cancer patient with suspected hypercalcaemia, why is it essential to calculate the corrected calcium level specifically using the serum albumin concentration?
options: Hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer and leads to underestimation of ionized calcium
Albumin acts as a competitive inhibitor of the parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP)
Hyperalbuminaemia is a pathognomonic feature of bone metastases in breast cancer
The parathyroid hormone only binds to the albumin-complexed fraction of serum calcium
Malignant tumors secrete albumin, which falsely lowers total calcium levels
correctOption: Hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer and leads to underestimation of ionized calcium
optionExplanations: Correct. Since a large portion of calcium is bound to albumin, low albumin levels result in a lower total calcium even if the physiologically active (ionized) calcium is high.
Albumin does not inhibit PTHrP; PTHrP acts on the PTH receptor independently of albumin levels.
Hyperalbuminaemia is rare in cancer; hypoalbuminaemia is the typical finding associated with advanced disease.
Ionized calcium (the unbound fraction) is the biologically active part regulated by PTH; total calcium measurement is simply confounded by albumin binding.
Cancer patients usually have low albumin (hypoalbuminaemia) due to cachexia or inflammation, not high albumin production.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 143 (Book Page): It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Which immunohistochemical (IHC) marker is utilized in clinical practice to indicate that a breast cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation?
optionExplanations: Correct. ER and PR positivity are the standard IHC markers for predicting response to endocrine (hormonal) therapies.
CD antigens are used for the diagnosis and classification of lymphomas.
EMA is used to favor a diagnosis of epithelial carcinoma in general.
HER2 indicates sensitivity to targeted HER2 inhibitors, not hormonal manipulation.
T-cell receptors are used in the classification of lymphomas, not breast cancer hormone sensitivity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Which imaging modality is considered the standard key investigation for initial staging and visualizing primary tumours within the thorax and abdomen?
optionExplanations: Isotope bone scans are used specifically for detecting bone metastases and do not provide visualization of primary soft tissue tumors in the thorax or abdomen.
PET visualises metabolic activity but is typically used in combination with CT (PET-CT) for specific assessments of metastasis rather than initial primary visualization.
Endoscopic ultrasound is a specialized tool helpful for staging upper gastrointestinal and pancreatic cancers, but not for broad thoraco-abdominal imaging.
MRI has high resolution but is primarily preferred for brain, bone, and pelvic imaging rather than initial broad staging of the thorax and abdomen.
CT is explicitly defined as the key investigation for imaging the thorax and abdomen in cancer patients.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): Computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation in cancer patients and is particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen (Fig. 7.5).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the evaluation of cancer spread, what is a primary factor that limits the sensitivity of Positron Emission Tomography (PET-CT) in identifying metastatic disease?
options: Frequent false-positive results occurring in necrotic tumour cores.
Inability to visualize the metabolic activity of non-avid tumours.
Poor anatomical resolution compared to standalone MRI scanners.
High radiation exposure limiting its use in longitudinal monitoring.
Failure to detect metabolic activity in small malignant lymph nodes.
correctOption: Failure to detect metabolic activity in small malignant lymph nodes.
optionExplanations: Necrotic cores typically show decreased metabolic activity (cold spots) rather than false positives in PET imaging.
While non-avid tumors are an issue, the text specifically identifies the failure to detect small malignant nodes as a sensitivity limitation.
PET-CT combines PET with CT to provide both metabolic and anatomical data; standalone resolution is not identified as the primary sensitivity limit here.
Radiation exposure is a consideration for CT-based imaging but is not the factor identified as limiting the sensitivity for metastasis detection in the source text.
The sensitivity of PET-CT is limited by the fact that it may not detect metabolic activity in nodes that are malignant but small.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): Not all tumour types are ‘PET-avid’ and the metabolic activity of small but malignant lymph nodes may not be detected, limiting the sensitivity of PET-CT.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: How does immunohistochemical (IHC) staining for the HER2 receptor directly influence the management plan for a patient diagnosed with breast cancer?
options: It predicts the likelihood of response to hormonal therapy manipulations.
It determines the clinical stage by identifying axillary node involvement.
It serves as a primary surrogate for evaluating the mitotic clock status.
It acts as a definitive marker for hereditary BRCA mutation syndromes.
It identifies whether the tumour may respond to targeted HER2 inhibitors.
correctOption: It identifies whether the tumour may respond to targeted HER2 inhibitors.
optionExplanations: Hormonal therapy sensitivity is predicted by ER (estrogen) and PR (progesterone) receptor positivity, not HER2.
Staging is determined by clinical examination, imaging, and surgical node sampling, not IHC markers like HER2.
The 'mitotic clock' refers to telomere shortening; IHC for HER2 does not measure replicative immortality or telomere status.
Hereditary syndromes are identified through genetic germline testing for mutations in genes like BRCA1 or BRCA2.
HER2 positivity is used to select patients for targeted therapies such as trastuzumab or other HER2 inhibitors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 68-year-old male presents with persistent lower back pain and fatigue. Imaging reveals multiple osteoblastic (blastic) lesions throughout the lumbar spine and pelvis. Laboratory tests show elevated alkaline phosphatase. According to high-yield diagnostic protocols for identifying the primary site in metastatic disease of unknown origin, which tumor marker is the most appropriate next step?
optionExplanations: hCG is checked in young men with midline disease or suspected germ cell tumors, not elderly men with blastic bone lesions.
CEA is a marker for colorectal or gastric cancers and is not the primary investigation for blastic bone metastases.
CA-125 is indicated for women with peritoneal malignancy or ascites, not for male bone metastases.
AFP is used for liver-limited disease or germ cell tumors, not typically for blastic bone lesions.
PSA is the investigation of choice for men presenting with bone lesions or blastic metastases to identify a prostate primary.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): Tumour markers: prostate-specific antigen (PSA) in men with bone lesions... (Box 7.11) and Page 139 (Book Page): Men with blastic bone metastases... Treat like prostate cancer (Box 7.12).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Molecular profiling of colorectal tumours for RAS mutations is routinely performed to guide treatment. What is the clinical significance of detecting a RAS mutation in these patients?
options: It suggests a strong sensitivity to platinum-based chemotherapy.
It confirms the presence of microsatellite instability in the cells.
It predicts a highly favorable response to ALK inhibitor therapy.
It identifies eligibility for checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy.
It indicates that the tumour will be resistant to EGFR inhibitors.
correctOption: It indicates that the tumour will be resistant to EGFR inhibitors.
optionExplanations: RAS status does not dictate sensitivity to platinum agents like oxaliplatin in the same way it does for targeted EGFR therapy.
Microsatellite instability is a separate molecular feature; RAS mutation status does not confirm its presence.
ALK fusion oncogene rearrangements predict response to ALK inhibitors, but this is primarily associated with lung cancer.
Eligibility for checkpoint inhibitors is typically predicted by microsatellite instability or PD-L1 expression, not RAS mutations.
In colon cancer, RAS mutations are a negative predictive marker, indicating that EGFR inhibitors (like cetuximab) will not be effective.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Using the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST), which findings define a partial response (PR) during the assessment of cancer treatment?
options: Complete disappearance of all target lesions noted at baseline.
At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameters.
At least a 20% increase in the sum of the longest diameters.
Total resolution of all target lesions and new metastatic nodes.
Neither sufficient shrinkage for PR nor sufficient growth for PD.
correctOption: At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameters.
optionExplanations: Disappearance of all target lesions defines a Complete Response (CR), not a Partial Response.
RECIST criteria define Partial Response as a 30% or greater reduction in the sum of the diameters of target lesions.
A 20% increase in the sum of longest diameters defines Progressive Disease (PD).
Resolution of lesions describes a Complete Response, whereas the appearance of new lesions would define Progressive Disease regardless of target lesion shrinkage.
Inability to meet criteria for shrinkage (PR) or growth (PD) defines Stable Disease (SD).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 148 (Book Page): Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: During the performance of a fine needle aspiration (FNA) of a palpable mass, what is the recommended action if blood is observed in the syringe hub?
options: Flush the hub with local anaesthetic to clear the cellular material.
Change the angle of the needle and continue making rapid passes.
Apply increased negative pressure to bypass the vascular area.
Immediately stop sampling as blood reduces the quality of the sample.
Continue the sampling until the syringe is half-full of liquid.
correctOption: Immediately stop sampling as blood reduces the quality of the sample.
optionExplanations: Hubs should not be flushed with anaesthetic; cellular material is expelled directly onto slides for evaluation.
Continuing the procedure after blood is visualized is contraindicated as the resulting specimen will be too bloody to read.
Increasing negative pressure would likely aspirate more blood, further compromising the biopsy specimen.
The standard protocol for FNA is to cease sampling once blood appears to ensure a high-quality cellular specimen.
Collecting large volumes of blood dilutes the cellular material and prevents accurate cytological evaluation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Stop sampling if blood is seen in the syringe hub as blood reduces the quality of the sample. (Box 7.5)

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 62-year-old female presents with progressively worsening dyspnoea and a non-productive cough. Physical examination reveals dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds at the lung base. Chest X-ray confirms a large pleural effusion. Which laboratory finding in the pleural fluid most strongly supports a malignant exudate?
options: A glucose level that is higher than the serum glucose level
A fluid-to-serum LDH ratio that is less than 0.6
A fluid-to-serum protein ratio that is greater than 0.5
A total protein level that is less than 30 grams per litre
A white blood cell count dominated by polymorphonuclears
correctOption: A fluid-to-serum protein ratio that is greater than 0.5
optionExplanations: Malignant effusions often have glucose levels lower than serum levels due to metabolic consumption by cancer cells or inflammatory cells.
A malignant exudate would show a fluid-to-serum LDH ratio greater than 0.6, not less.
Malignant effusions are typically exudates, defined by a fluid-to-serum protein ratio greater than 0.5.
Exudates generally have higher protein levels (typically >30 g/L); levels <30 g/L are more characteristic of transudates.
While white cells may be present, a polymorphonuclear-dominated count is more suggestive of acute infection (parapneumonic) than malignancy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 144 (Book Page): Malignant effusions are commonly blood-stained and are exudates with a raised fluid to serum LDH ratio (> 0.6) and a raised fluid to serum protein ratio (> 0.5).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: When measuring serum calcium levels in cancer patients to diagnose hypercalcaemia, why is it essential to adjust the total calcium value for albumin levels?
options: Albumin competes with calcium for renal tubular reabsorption in the kidneys.
Total calcium levels are only accurate when the albumin concentration is above 45 g/L.
Hypoalbuminaemia is common and causes total calcium to underestimate ionised calcium.
Albumin acts as a buffering agent that neutralizes the effects of ectopic PTH secretion.
High albumin levels often falsely elevate the measured ionised calcium fraction.
correctOption: Hypoalbuminaemia is common and causes total calcium to underestimate ionised calcium.
optionExplanations: Albumin does not compete with calcium for renal reabsorption; the primary issue is its role as a carrier protein in the blood.
Accuracy isn't limited to specific concentrations, but corrections are required across the range when albumin is abnormal.
Since much of serum calcium is protein-bound, low albumin leads to a lower total calcium measurement despite the physiological active (ionised) calcium potentially being high.
Albumin does not neutralize PTHrP or PTH; its role in this context is purely as a transport protein influencing blood tests.
Albumin level does not falsely elevate ionised calcium; it affects the total calcium measurement. High albumin would lead to overestimation of the calcium status.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: Which of the following chromosomal translocations is characteristically detected using fluorescent in situ hybridisation (FISH) to aid in the diagnosis of Ewing's sarcoma?
optionExplanations: The t(11;22) translocation is the diagnostic hallmark for Ewing's sarcoma and peripheral neuro-ectodermal tumours.
t(8;14) is characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma, not Ewing's sarcoma.
t(9;22) is the Philadelphia chromosome, characteristic of Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia.
t(15;17) is the hallmark of Acute Promyelocytic Leukaemia (APL).
t(14;18) is commonly associated with follicular lymphoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): The utilisation of fluorescent in situ hybridisation (FISH) techniques can be useful in Ewing's sarcoma... where there is a translocation between chromosome 11 and 22: t(11;22)(q24;q12).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the standard T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach developed by the International Union against Cancer (UICC), what specific aspect of the disease is categorized by the 'N' component?
options: The presence of distant metastases in other organs.
The overall depth of invasion of the primary tumor.
The metabolic activity of the primary malignant lesion.
The involvement of regional lymph nodes by cancer.
The histological grade of the malignant cells identified.
correctOption: The involvement of regional lymph nodes by cancer.
optionExplanations: Metastatic sites (distant spread) are categorized by the 'M' component of the TNM system.
The size or depth of invasion of the primary tumor is categorized by the 'T' component.
Metabolic activity is a feature assessed by functional imaging like PET, not by the anatomical TNM staging categories.
According to Box 7.3 and the UICC guidelines, the 'N' component specifically records the regional lymph node involvement.
Histological grading is a separate pathological assessment and is not part of the basic TNM anatomical staging.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC, see Box 7.3).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: How does the clinical utilization of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) primarily differ from Computed Tomography (CT) in the staging and evaluation of malignant disease?
options: It evaluates blood flow velocity within the tumor's neovascular network.
It uses ionizing radiation to measure bone density in metastatic sites.
It provides superior anatomical detail of the surrounding soft tissue.
It relies on acoustic impedance to differentiate between cystic and solid masses.
It visualizes the metabolic activity of tumor cells rather than anatomy.
correctOption: It visualizes the metabolic activity of tumor cells rather than anatomy.
optionExplanations: Evaluating blood flow velocity is typically performed using Doppler ultrasound or specific MRI sequences.
CT and X-rays use ionizing radiation for structure; PET uses radiopharmaceuticals to track metabolism.
Anatomical detail is the strength of CT and MRI; PET provides functional/metabolic information.
Differentiating cystic and solid masses via acoustic impedance is the principle of ultrasound, not PET.
PET is unique in its ability to visualize metabolic activity, which is useful for detecting active disease that may not yet show anatomical changes on CT.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A clinician is determining the most appropriate imaging modality for a patient with a suspected primary brain tumor and potential bone marrow involvement. Which technique is preferred due to its high resolution in these specific regions?
options: Radionuclide isotope bone scanning with technetium.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the affected sites.
Positron emission tomography with glucose markers.
correctOption: Magnetic resonance imaging of the affected sites.
optionExplanations: Ultrasound is preferred for liver, kidney, pancreas, and reproductive organs, not for intra-cranial or bone imaging.
CT is useful for thorax and abdomen but lacks the soft tissue resolution of MRI for brain and bone marrow.
Isotope bone scans are sensitive for detecting osteoblastic activity but have lower resolution and specificity compared to MRI.
MRI is the gold standard for brain and bone imaging due to its high resolution and superior soft-tissue contrast.
PET is used for metabolic staging of the whole body but is not the primary high-resolution modality for brain or bone structure.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Diagnostic Pathway for Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP)
statement: A 45-year-old female presents with a firm, non-tender, palpable mass in her right axilla. A core biopsy of the mass reveals adenocarcinoma, but no primary lesion is identified on clinical examination of the breasts or a subsequent mammogram. According to the systematic approach for cancer of unknown primary, what is the most appropriate next investigation to identify the primary site?
options: Diagnostic laparoscopy to visualize the peritoneal surfaces.
Magnetic resonance imaging of both the breast tissues.
High-resolution computed tomography of the chest and neck.
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography for the biliary tree.
correctOption: Magnetic resonance imaging of both the breast tissues.
optionExplanations: Laparoscopy is indicated for peritoneal malignancy or ascites, not for isolated axillary adenopathy.
In cases of isolated axillary adenocarcinoma where mammography is negative, Breast MRI is specifically indicated to detect occult primary breast cancer.
PET-CT may be used later, but specific imaging for the most likely primary (breast) is indicated first in isolated axillary nodes.
CT of the chest/abdomen/pelvis is a baseline, but in this specific scenario, a targeted Breast MRI is the specialized next step.
ERCP is used for biliary or pancreatic pathologies and is not part of the standard workup for axillary node adenocarcinoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 140 (Book Page): Box 7.11: Breast MRI for women with adenocarcinoma limited to axillary nodes.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the context of histopathology and immunohistochemistry (IHC), which staining profile is most helpful in predicting whether a breast cancer patient will respond to targeted therapy with human epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitors?
options: Positive expression of T-cell receptors and CD antigens.
High levels of estrogen and progesterone receptor expression.
Presence of cytokeratins and epithelial membrane antigen.
Evidence of HER2 receptor positivity on tumor cell membranes.
Identification of alpha-fetoprotein within the tumor cells.
correctOption: Evidence of HER2 receptor positivity on tumor cell membranes.
optionExplanations: CD antigens and T-cell receptors are used for classifying lymphomas, not for guiding breast cancer targeted therapy.
ER/PR positivity indicates sensitivity to hormonal manipulation, not necessarily to HER2 inhibitors.
Cytokeratins and EMA favor epithelial carcinomas generally but do not predict specific drug responses.
HER2 positivity on IHC (or FISH) is the prerequisite for using HER2 inhibitors like trastuzumab.
AFP favors germ-cell or hepatocellular tumors and is not relevant to targeted breast cancer therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: How is a patient's performance status classified on the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale if they are capable of only limited self-care and spend more than 50% of their waking hours confined to a bed or chair?
optionExplanations: Grade 4 refers to patients who are completely disabled and totally confined to a bed or chair.
Grade 0 refers to a patient who is fully active and able to carry on all usual activities without restriction.
Grade 2 refers to patients who are ambulatory and capable of self-care but up and about more than 50% of waking hours.
Grade 1 refers to patients restricted in strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out light work.
Grade 3 specifically describes patients capable of limited self-care who are confined to bed/chair more than 50% of waking hours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): Box 7.6: 3 Capable of only limited self-care, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 60-year-old female with a history of cirrhosis presents with new-onset ascites. A serum investigation reveals a significantly elevated Cancer Antigen 125 (CA-125). In this clinical context, how should the CA-125 elevation be interpreted by the medical team?
options: It may be elevated due to the presence of ascites of any cause.
It is specific for gastrointestinal or colorectal cancer spread.
It is diagnostic of an underlying ovarian epithelial malignancy.
It is the only marker required to determine the disease stage.
It indicates a favorable response to previous systemic treatment.
correctOption: It may be elevated due to the presence of ascites of any cause.
optionExplanations: CA-125 is notoriously non-specific and can be raised in benign conditions causing peritoneal or pleural irritation, such as ascites from cirrhosis.
CA-19.9 or CEA are more associated with gastrointestinal cancers; CA-125 is a differentiation antigen of coelomic epithelium.
While common in ovarian cancer, CA-125 is not diagnostic as it is poorly specific.
Stage is determined by imaging and physical exam (TNM), never by a single serum tumor marker.
Elevated markers usually indicate disease presence or progression, not a favorable response.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): Box 7.4: Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125)... Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 62-year-old male with known metastatic prostate cancer presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of band-like thoracic back pain, progressive lower limb weakness, and urinary retention. What is the most critical next investigative step to confirm the suspected clinical diagnosis?
options: Urgent magnetic resonance imaging scan of the entire spinal column.
Computed tomography of the head to exclude intracranial lesions.
Serum prostate-specific antigen level to assess disease progression.
Isotope bone scan to identify new osteoblastic skeletal metastases.
Plain film radiographs of the thoracic and lumbar vertebral bodies.
correctOption: Urgent magnetic resonance imaging scan of the entire spinal column.
optionExplanations: Urgent MRI of the whole spine is the definitive gold-standard investigation for suspected malignant spinal cord compression.
The clinical findings are distal to the head (lower limb weakness, urinary retention), pointing to a spinal, not cerebral, lesion.
PSA monitors disease activity but is not a diagnostic tool for the acute anatomical emergency of cord compression.
Bone scans detect turnover but cannot confirm cord compression or visualize the soft tissue impingement on the spinal cord.
Plain films can show bone destruction but lack the sensitivity to diagnose spinal cord compression.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): Box 7.14: Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the molecular profiling of solid tumors, identifying which specific genomic aberration in a colorectal cancer biopsy is a key predictor of resistance to targeted therapy using Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) inhibitors?
options: Amplication of the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2.
Presence of the ALK fusion oncogene rearrangement in tissue.
Loss of the TP53 tumour suppressor gene function in the tumor.
Mutations within the RAS family of genes (e.g., KRAS or NRAS).
Expression of the programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) protein.
correctOption: Mutations within the RAS family of genes (e.g., KRAS or NRAS).
optionExplanations: HER2 amplification is relevant in breast and gastric cancer therapy, but RAS is the key predictive marker for EGFR inhibitors in colon cancer.
ALK fusion rearrangements are predictive for ALK inhibitors in lung cancer, not for EGFR inhibitors in colon cancer.
TP53 mutations are common across many cancers but do not specifically predict resistance to anti-EGFR therapy in the clinical setting.
Identifying RAS mutations is essential in colon cancer as they predict a lack of response (resistance) to EGFR inhibitors like cetuximab.
PD-L1 expression is a biomarker for immunotherapy (checkpoint inhibitors), not for EGFR targeted therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 138 (Book Page): RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: During the light microscopic examination of a diagnostic biopsy sample, the identification of signet-ring cells is a histopathological finding that strongly suggests which of the following primary tumor sites?
options: Squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx.
Primary malignant melanoma of the skin.
Papillary cell carcinoma of the thyroid.
Serous papillary adenocarcinoma of the ovary.
optionExplanations: Squamous cell carcinomas are characterized by keratin pearls or intercellular bridges, not signet-ring morphology.
Melanoma is characterized by the presence of melanin and specific cellular morphology, not signet-ring cells.
Thyroid cancer is often associated with Psammoma bodies (if papillary) or specific follicular patterns.
Ovarian cancer is more commonly associated with mucin and Psammoma bodies.
Signet-ring cells are a classic histopathological hallmark favoring a primary gastric adenocarcinoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: In the standard TNM staging system used by the International Union against Cancer (UICC), how is the specific presence of distant metastatic spread formally categorized?
options: Categorized as MX when there is no evidence of tumor spread beyond lymph nodes
Categorized as M1 when the tumor has spread to anatomically distant sites
Categorized as T0 when no primary tumor is identified during initial imaging
Categorized as NX when the regional lymph nodes cannot be clinically assessed
Categorized as T4 when the primary tumor increases in size or depth of invasion
correctOption: Categorized as M1 when the tumor has spread to anatomically distant sites
optionExplanations: MX indicates that the presence of distant metastases could not be assessed, whereas M0 indicates they are not present.
According to the UICC TNM system, M1 is the specific designation indicating that distant metastases are present.
T0 indicates no evidence of a primary tumor, not the categorization for distant metastasis.
NX refers to the inability to assess regional lymph nodes, which is distinct from distant metastatic spread.
T4 refers to the extent of the primary tumor (size or local invasion), whereas metastases are handled by the M category.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): [Presence of metastases MX Not assessed M0 Not present M1 Present]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A patient undergoes a Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scan as part of a staging workup. Which physiological property of the tumor is primarily visualized by this imaging modality?
options: The acoustic impedance of the tumor compared to adjacent normal viscera
The resonance of hydrogen nuclei within the extracellular fluid of the mass
The biochemical metabolic activity occurring within the malignant cells
The vascular density and blood flow patterns surrounding a primary lesion
The anatomical resolution of tumor margins within soft tissue structures
correctOption: The biochemical metabolic activity occurring within the malignant cells
optionExplanations: Acoustic impedance is the property utilized in ultrasound imaging, not positron emission tomography.
The resonance of hydrogen nuclei is the underlying principle of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), not PET.
PET scans specifically visualize the metabolic activity of cells, which is typically higher in malignant tissues.
While metabolic activity is related to blood flow, PET specifically measures biochemical turnover (e.g., glucose) rather than vascular density.
PET is often combined with CT (PET-CT) because PET itself has lower anatomical resolution compared to CT or MRI.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: When determining the most appropriate imaging modality for a patient suspected of having a pelvic malignancy, which factor makes Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) the preferred technique over Computed Tomography (CT)?
options: MRI allows for better preparation of the large bowel for luminal detection
MRI provides superior visualization of the thorax and abdominal viscera
MRI is the preferred technique for bone, brain, and pelvic site imaging
MRI has a higher resolution for detecting metabolic activity in small nodes
MRI utilizes ionizing radiation which is more effective for dense pelvic bone
correctOption: MRI is the preferred technique for bone, brain, and pelvic site imaging
optionExplanations: CT colonography is the technique used for visualizing the large bowel if it is prepared, not MRI.
CT is noted as being particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen, whereas MRI is preferred for the pelvis.
MRI is specifically highlighted as the preferred technique for imaging the brain, bone, and pelvis due to its high resolution.
PET-CT is used for metabolic activity; MRI is chosen for its high anatomical resolution and soft tissue contrast.
MRI does not use ionizing radiation; it uses magnetic fields and radio waves, which is one of its clinical advantages.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 68-year-old male presents with painless jaundice, significant weight loss, and a palpable epigastric mass. A CT scan reveals a 3 cm mass in the head of the pancreas with dilated bile ducts. Which investigative approach would most accurately facilitate both the staging of the local tumor and the acquisition of a tissue biopsy?
options: Isotope bone scan to detect osteoblastic activity indicating distant metastases
Fine needle aspiration of a palpable lymph node in the supraclavicular area
Endoscopic ultrasound utilizing a specialized probe with a biopsy attachment
Computed tomography-guided percutaneous biopsy of the pancreatic head mass
Diagnostic laparoscopy to visualize peritoneal washings for malignant cells
correctOption: Endoscopic ultrasound utilizing a specialized probe with a biopsy attachment
optionExplanations: A bone scan evaluates distant spread to the skeletal system but does not aid in the primary diagnosis or local staging of the pancreatic mass.
While supraclavicular nodes (Virchow's node) can be aspirated if present, endoscopic ultrasound is the specific tool for pancreatic staging and biopsy.
Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) is specifically recommended for staging and biopsying pancreatic cancers because the probe can get close to the organ.
CT-guided biopsy is possible, but EUS is superior for staging the local extent of pancreatic and upper GI cancers.
Laparoscopy is used for staging the extent of disease (e.g., peritoneal spread) but is less common for the primary biopsy of the pancreatic head.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Endoscopic ultrasound is helpful in staging upper gastrointestinal and pancreatic cancers, involving a special endoscope with an ultrasound and biopsy probe attached.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
statement: A 55-year-old woman is being evaluated for a newly discovered adnexal mass. The clinician orders a serum Cancer Antigen 125 (CA-125) level. Which limitation must the clinician consider when interpreting a raised CA-125 in this patient?
options: CA-125 is a human leucocyte antigen fragment found only on epithelial cells
CA-125 is sensitive enough to be used as a standalone diagnostic tool for cancer
CA-125 can be raised in any condition causing ascites, such as heart failure
CA-125 levels are exclusively eliminated via the biliary system causing false rises
CA-125 is only elevated in patients with non-seminomatous germ cell tumors
correctOption: CA-125 can be raised in any condition causing ascites, such as heart failure
optionExplanations: Beta-2-microglobulin is the fragment of the human leucocyte antigen (HLA) mentioned in the text.
The text states that most tumor markers are neither sufficiently sensitive nor specific to be used in isolation for diagnosis.
CA-125 is non-specific as it can be elevated in various inflammatory conditions, ascites, or heart failure, requiring clinical context.
CA-19.9 is the marker noted for being eliminated exclusively via bile, making it sensitive to cholestasis.
AFP and hCG are the markers associated with germ cell tumors; CA-125 is associated with ovarian epithelial cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): [Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. Can be raised in inflammatory conditions Ovarian epithelial cancer (75%), gastrointestinal cancer (10%)]
